 Judgment

This is a petition filed u/s. 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 25-3-2022 at about 3.00 p.m. when the petitioner was pedestrian near St.Antony's church Gangodanahalli main road, Gangodanahalli, Bengaluru at that time, driver of the car bearing No.KA-16-M-4629 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, due to which petitioner had sustained grievous injuries and took treatment at hospital as inpatient and spent huge amount towards his treatment.

It is further stated that petitioner is aged 34 years, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and was working as fish seller and earning Rs.25,000/-p.m. and due to accidental injuries, he is unable to do any work and not in a position to attend to his work and sustained loss of income.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents.
3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsel and only respondent No.2 filed written statement.

4. Respondent No.2 filed written statement wherein contended that petitioner was negligent in walking almost at the middle of the road with his pulling cart and was moving on the road without observing the on coming traffic.
The accident if any has occurred only due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
The owner/insured has not intimated about the accident to insurance company.
The complaint is lodged by the petitioner in the police station on 31-3-2022 at 12.30 p.m. after 7 days of the accident and there is a 7 days delay in filing the complaint.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant and disproportionate to the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
Hence prays to dismiss the claim petition.

5. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing reg.No.KA-16-M-4629 on 25-3-2022 at about 3.00 p.m. near St.Antony's church, Gangodanahalli main road, Gangodanahalli, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?

6. The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and Exs.P1 to P12 documents are marked.
On the other hand, respondents have not led their defence evidence.

7. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:

In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 12 documents as Ex-P1 to 12 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, col.133 notice,
reply, IMV report, charge sheet, wound certificate, OPD record, Adhaar card, x-ray.
10. The evidence on record reveals that petitioner himself has lodged the complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle before the Byatarayanapura traffic police as per Ex-P2.

Thereafter jurisdictional police got registered FIR and conducted the thorough investigation and filed the charge sheet at Ex.P8 against the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-16-M-4629 for the offences punishable U/s 279, 338 of I.P.C. by holding that on 25-3-2022 at about 3 p.m. the driver of the car bearing No.KA-16-M-4629 drove the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human being from Ganapathi circle towards Nayandahalli by pushing his push cart, who was moving infront of him and thereby caused the accident.
Due to the accident, petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
On perusal of the cross- examination of the PW-1, it is pertinent to note here that no where respondent No.2 has seriously disputed the occurrence of the accident.

Counsel for the respondent has taken the contention that accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligence of the petitioner himself as he came to the middle of the road and there was a footpath,
petitioner would have taken his push cart on the side of the road.
In this regard, counsel for the respondent No.2 cross examined PW-1 at length.
Wherein counsel for the respondent No.2 suggested that as petitioner was going on the middle of the road, accident had been taken place which has been outrightly denied by the PW-1.
Except the above said suggestion there is nothing forthcoming from the cross examination of PW-1 which supports the defence taken by the respondent No.2.
In this regard, on perusal of the spot mahazar, Ex-P3 and 4 sketch, it clearly shows that spot of accident is a main road having two way direction.
Further there is a cross road and also there is a footpath road on both side and accident had been taken place on the left edge of the vehicle proceeding from Ganapathi circle towards Nayandahalli.

Admittedly both car and the petitioner was moving on the same direction and Ex- P4 clearly shows that there is a sufficient space on the road for the driver of the offending vehicle to move on the other side of road.

Ex-P4 clearly Vazir Pasha vs Dean And Campus Head Post on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146054057/
3 shows that the accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Moreover the respondent except the suggestion, has not examined the driver of the offending vehicle to disprove the evidence of the petitioner and to establish his defence.
The driver of the offending vehicle is a material witness to state facts and circumstances under which the accident had been caused.

11. Further respondent has taken the contention that accident had been occurred on 25-03-2022 at 3.00 p.m., but the petitioner has lodged the complaint on 31-03-2022 at 12.30 p.m. and admittedly there is a delay of 7 days in lodging the complaint.
In this regard, PW-1 himself in cross examination has clearly stated that as he was under treatment and he was not able to walk, lodged the complaint belatedly.

Even petitioner in his complaint Ex-P2 has stated that as the driver of the vehicle has agreed to lookafter all his medical expenses and requested the PW-1 not to lodge the complaint but later on driver of the offending vehicle did not come and lookafter his medical expenses and hence thereafter petitioner himself has lodged the complaint against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Even in ExP1 also the reason for the delay is stated as earlier driver of the respondent has agreed to lookafter the medical expenses, but later on denied.
Hence there is a delay of 7 days.

On perusal of Ex-P9 wound certificate, it clearly shows that petitioner was admitted to the hospital soon after the accident on 25-3-2022 at around 3.00 p.m. near Chandra layout while the petitioner was moving the push cart hit by four wheeler and ran over his left ankle and above said injuries are grievous in nature.
Even Ex-P10 the medical certificate of the doctor clearly states that on 25-3- 2022 petitioner has met with an accident and he was hit by the four wheeler and ran over his left ankle.
All these documents also have not at all been disputed by the respondents.

All the police documents clearly establish that there was a accident between the petitioner and the offending vehicle on 25-3-2022 and petitioner for the reason stated by him might have lodged the complaint belatedly.
12. There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Ex.P7 IMV report indicates that the occurrence of the said accident was not due to any of the mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident.

13. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
14. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle car bearing No.KA-16-M-4629.

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
16. ISSUE NO.2:
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing No.KA-16-M- 4629.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
17. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 34 years.
From the Ex-P11- Aadhaar card it reveals that his date of birth is 1-1-1987.
Hence, petitioner was aged 35 years.
Hence as on the date of accident i.e.,2022, petitioner was aged about 35 years.
The petitioner has stated that he was fish seller and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,500/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
18. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove his disability.
Therefore this tribunal is not awarding compensation under the head loss of future income due to disability.

19. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the Ex-P9-wound certificate the petitioner has sustained injuries (1) right supraorbital ridge scar mark and (2) right lower anterior and as per the opinion of doctor, the said injuries are grievous in nature,

The petitioner has not produced discharge summary and the bills and even not examined the doctor inspite of it,
looking into the injuries of the petitioner, as per ex-P9 wound certificate of Star Ortho and Shashi Fertility center, petitioner needs open reduction and internal fixation operation but persons with the petitioner were not willing for payment for the surgery and hence they were treated conservatively.

entities.text: Star Ortho and Shashi Fertility center
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Even there are no materials on record to show that petitioner underwent any surgery or taken any treatment.
As per Ex-P9 petitioner had sustained grievous injuries and sustained fracture.
Hence petitioner might have taken two months for recovery from the injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 35 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

20. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:

sentences.text: By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him as conservatively and it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 2 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.31,000/- (15,500 X 2) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
21. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is residing in Gangondanahalli, Bangalore and has taken treatment at Star Ortho and Shashi Fertility center, Nagarbhavi, Bengaluru.

entities.text: Star Ortho and Shashi Fertility center, Nagarbhavi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Admittedly, petitioner has not produced any documents to show that he was admitted in the hospital to show that he has spent any amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence no compensation is awarded under this head.

22. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded under this head.
23. MEDICAL EXPENSES.
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner has not produced medical bills and prescriptions.
Hence, this tribunal is not awarding compensation under the head of medical expenses.

24. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Pain & sufferings : 50,000=00 2 Loss of income during : 31,000=00 laid-up period 3 Loss of future amenities : 10,000=00 & happiness Total 91,000=00 25. INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
26. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle car bearing No.KA-16-M-4629. and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date Vazir Pasha vs Dean And Campus Head Post on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146054057/
6 of this order.

27. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.91,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
